about: r11-9: 'not sent' versus 'may have been sent' is the core's rule, from the error CLASS a shell passes (`rpc_pool::TransportFailure`, uniffi/wasm `transport_outcome_of` / `transportOutcomeOf`). A refused connect, a name that did not resolve, a TLS failure, a request the platform refused to send or one that never left whole reached nobody: a submit that met only those is `not_sent` ('try again'). Only a request that left whole may have been acted on: `maybe_sent` ('don't send it again'). The round-11 Android send was refused by the relay's host in 4–6 ms and said maybe_sent. `outcome` is the pool's `RpcTransportOutcome`; `may_have_delivered` is `rpc_pool::may_have_delivered` of it; `submit` is `user_op::submit_step(NoAnswer, 0, may_have_delivered, …)`'s verdict type. Each shell's test maps its own platform errors to these classes (`platform` lists the usual ones per shell, as guidance — the classes are the contract). Replayed by rust/crates/vela-core/tests/app_fee_parity.rs.

platform.android: ConnectException, NoRouteToHostException; okhttp connectFailed before any request byte

platform.ios: URLError.badURL / .unsupportedURL / ATS / a proxy refusing CONNECT

platform.android: an IOException after connectEnd and before requestBodyEnd (okhttp EventListener)
an IOException after requestBodyEnd: reset, 'unexpected end of stream'
platform.ios: URLError.networkConnectionLost after the body was sent

platform.android: SocketTimeoutException reading the answer; okhttp's call timeout after the request

platform.web: a thrown fetch while online — fetch cannot say how far it got
